gen-silkscreen-fs-asap: Silkscreen spaces its pixel letters so loosely you can nearly feel the gaps. Asap, a sans-serif with open-arc curves and lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, gives that retro quirkiness a sturdy, readable partner.
gen-silkscreen-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Retro and lo-fi, Silkscreen feels like a game screen. Be Vietnam Pro, a sans-serif with a high mean line and curve endings that stay well apart, is far larger in presence, so a shrunken heading would get swallowed by it.
gen-silkscreen-fs-epilogue: Approachable curves in Epilogue, with a tall-bodied lowercase and stubby ascender tips, sit beneath Silkscreen's lo-fi, spaced-out pixel lettering. Each keeps its own voice.
gen-silkscreen-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans reads large and friendly, with a tall x-height and s curves that open wide at both ends. Silkscreen sits above it as the retro, lo-fi counterweight, a display face whose spaced-out letters make the sans-serif below look even sturdier.
gen-silkscreen-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans reads sturdy and large, its tall lowercase and clearly open e making words look broad and solid. Silkscreen's thin, uniform bars are the foil.
gen-silkscreen-fs-public-sans: Public Sans brings a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, so text feels trustworthy and solid on the page. And Silkscreen, lo-fi and retro, adds its spaced-out pixel lines on top, keeping a longer passage grounded while the heading has fun.
gen-silkscreen-general-sans: Clean and professional, General Sans fills the line with a tall x-height and smooth curves that flow around each bend. And Silkscreen earns its keep when big and short, where its spaced-out retro letters get room to show off.
gen-silkscreen-gf-orbit: Orbit keeps every stem, bowl and tail rope-like in consistency, with curves that stop short and characters floating apart. And Silkscreen does the loud, lo-fi, retro heading work, while Orbit handles the quieter job of being a sans text face.
gen-silkscreen-gf-science-gothic: Science Gothic keeps its stroke ends far apart and its lines without thick or thin parts, so reading feels like taking in one letter at a time. Silkscreen is the better shouter, with retro, spaced-out letters, while Science Gothic is the better talker.
gen-silkscreen-gf-syncopate: Silkscreen brings lo-fi, retro pixel letters with space you can almost feel around each one. Syncopate follows with open shapes and technical-pen steadiness, its rope-ladder spacing giving the sans text a measured, precise stride beneath the heading.
